articles.title: Oli calls September 9 a day of ‘horrific destruction’, questions why accused remain free
articles.summary: Former Prime Minister and CPN‑UML chair KP Sharma Oli labeled September 9, 2025, as a day of “horrific destruction,” condemning the violence that followed Gen Z protests as a major assault on Nepal’s state institutions, democracy and economy. In a video message released on the anniversary, Oli questioned why those accused of the unrest remain free, urging accountability and highlighting the lasting impact on the nation’s stability.

articles.title: Rabi Lamichhane to address Parliament on Bhotekoshi flood response
articles.summary: Rastriya Swatantra Party chair Rabi Lamichhane will speak in the House of Representatives on Wednesday about the government's response to the catastrophic Bhotekoshi River flood in Rasuwa district. He plans to discuss ongoing search and rescue missions, relief distribution, and rehabilitation measures for the affected communities. The address underscores the urgency of coordinated action to aid victims and restore the region after the severe flooding that caused widespread damage.

articles.title: What Nepal lost in two days of Gen Z unrest
articles.summary: Two days of Gen Z unrest in Kathmandu left lasting damage to Nepal’s key government infrastructure. The Prime Minister’s Office at Singha Durbar remains in ruins, and reconstruction of the Birendra International Convention Centre in New Baneshwor has not yet started. The article reflects on the broader losses incurred by the nation, highlighting the visible scars on important state buildings a year after the protests and questioning the long‑term impact on governance and public services.

articles.title: UML calls Gen Z uprising a ‘serious attack’ on democracy and national economy
articles.summary: The Communist Party of Nepal – Unified Marxist Leninist (CPN‑UML) has labeled the September 8‑9 Gen Z protests in Kathmandu as a "serious attack" on Nepal's democracy, national economy and state foundations. In a statement issued on September 9, the party condemned the unrest, which resulted in the deaths of several young demonstrators during police action, and paid tribute to the victims. The party warned that such uprisings threaten the country's stability and development.

articles.title: Both houses of Federal Parliament to meet today
articles.summary: Both houses of Nepal's Federal Parliament are set to convene on Wednesday, with the House of Representatives scheduled to begin at 1 pm at Singha Durbar in Kathmandu. The session will consider two bills and a proposal concerning Nepal's membership in an Asian legislative body. Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Sobita will oversee the proceedings.

articles.title: Climate justice is still far away for Nepal
articles.summary: The Bhotekoshi flood, triggered by a massive rock‑and‑ice avalanche, devastated the Bhotekoshi‑Trishuli river system in Nepal, killing people, destroying homes and critical infrastructure within minutes. The disaster highlights the growing and unequal climate risks faced by Himalayan nations and underscores the lack of climate justice for Nepal. The article argues that despite the severity of such events, Nepal remains distant from meaningful climate justice measures, calling for urgent international attention and support to address the mounting environmental threats in the region.

articles.title: Landslide-blocked Kimrong Khola reopens, immediate risk subsides
articles.summary: The Kimrong Khola river in Pokhara, Kaski, which was blocked by a landslide on Tuesday night in Annapurna Rural Municipality-11, has naturally reopened, reducing immediate flood risk. Kaski Assistant Chief District Officer Chitrangal Baral confirmed the blockage cleared on its own. Authorities are monitoring the situation, but the immediate danger to downstream communities has subsided.

articles.title: Landslide blocks Kimrong Khola in Kaski, residents urged to move to safety
articles.summary: A landslide has blocked the Kimrong Khola river in Annapurna Rural Municipality-11 of Kaski district, Nepal. The blockage, which occurred about six hours before the report, prompted Kaski District Police Chief SP Navin Karki to advise residents of nearby settlements to relocate to safer areas. Authorities are monitoring the situation and urging prompt evacuation to prevent potential flooding or further hazards caused by the landslide.

articles.title: Prachanda accuses government of hiding Gen Z movement probe report
articles.summary: Pushpa Kamal Dahal, known as Prachanda and coordinator of the Nepal Communist Party, alleged that the government has concealed the investigation report on last year’s Gen Z movement. Speaking at a memorial gathering in Sindhupalchok, he claimed officials have deliberately kept the findings from the public, suggesting a lack of transparency and accountability. The accusation adds to ongoing political tension surrounding the youth protests and raises questions about governmental handling of the probe.

articles.title: What rescue teams found and how far they searched in hydropower tunnels today
articles.summary: Search and rescue teams, including the Nepal Army, are continuing operations in the Rasuwagadhi and other hydropower projects in Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts after severe flooding of the Bhotekoshi River. The joint teams are probing tunnels and other structures to locate workers still missing following the disaster. The article details how far the teams have progressed in their searches and what, if any, remains have been found, highlighting the ongoing challenges of the rescue effort.

articles.title: GCEF launches national Teej cultural campaign to support flood relief
articles.summary: The Global Cultural Expedition Foundation (GCEF) has launched a nationwide school and college cultural competition called “GCEF Teej for Nepal 2026 — National School & College Cultural Championship.” The event, timed with the Teej festival, aims to showcase student talent and Nepali cultural traditions while raising support for communities still recovering from recent floods. Participants from across Nepal will compete in various cultural categories, with proceeds or donations directed toward flood‑relief initiatives.

articles.title: Mamaearth contributes Rs 2.1 million to Nepal disaster relief fund
articles.summary: Personal care brand Mamaearth donated Rs 2.1 million to Nepal’s Prime Minister’s Natural Disaster Relief Fund to aid families affected by recent floods. The contribution was handed over by Sawan Jaiswal, General Manager of Mamaearth Nepal, to Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle in Kathmandu. The donation is part of the company’s corporate social responsibility efforts to support disaster‑relief initiatives in the country.

articles.title: Daily Digest: The biggest stories, developments and updates of the day
articles.summary: The Daily Digest from OnlineKhabar English News compiles the most significant stories of the day, covering Nepal’s current affairs, international developments, business, sports, and in‑depth features. Among the highlighted items is the recent deposit of nearly Rs 12 billion into the Prime Minister’s relief fund. The digest aims to provide readers with a concise overview of key events and updates.

articles.title: Nearly Rs 12 billion deposited in Prime Minister’s relief funds
articles.summary: The Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers reported that nearly Rs 12 billion (Rs 11.77 billion as of 9 am on Tuesday) has been deposited into the Prime Minister’s Disaster Relief Fund and the Prime Minister’s Relief Fund. The funds are intended to support disaster response and other relief activities across Nepal. The announcement was made in Kathmandu on September 8.

articles.title: Nepal’s youth revolt, a year later
articles.summary: A year after the September Storm protests in Kathmandu, Nepal's youth reflect on the deadly rally that sparked a nationwide revolt. The article revisits the events that turned violent, examines the government's response, and discusses the social and political changes that have emerged since. Students recount personal losses, ongoing demands for education reform, and their hopes for a more inclusive political landscape. While some progress is noted, many still feel the promises remain unfulfilled, highlighting the lingering tension between the younger generation and the establishment.

articles.title: 3 Nepalis arrested in Japan over murder of Nepali woman
articles.summary: Three Nepali nationals have been detained by Japanese police in connection with the killing of 25‑year‑old Nepali woman Laxmi Rajbanshi in Fukuoka, Japan. The suspects are 28‑year‑old Sanju Tamang, a vocational‑school student in Hakata Ward, and 25‑year‑old Amista Tamang, a resident of Tosu, along with a third individual whose details were not disclosed. The arrests were made on murder charges, and the case has drawn attention from both Nepalese and Japanese media.

articles.title: Researcher claims exceptional heat preceded glacier collapse that triggered deadly Rasuwa floods
articles.summary: A researcher analysing meteorological data reports that the glacier at 5,200 m altitude, whose collapse caused the deadly floods in Rasuwa, Nepal and parts of China on August 26, experienced unusually high temperatures in the days leading up to the event, with average readings around 5 °C. The study suggests that this exceptional heat may have contributed to the glacier’s failure, highlighting the role of extreme weather in triggering such disasters.

articles.title: Israel opens applications for 1,464 Nepali care workers
articles.summary: The Department of Foreign Employment in Nepal has announced that applications are now open for 1,464 Nepali workers to serve as caregivers in Israel's long‑term care centres for individuals with severe disabilities. The recruitment includes 1,132 women and 332 men. Applicants must meet specified eligibility criteria and will be deployed to Israel to provide care for people of all ages with disabilities.

articles.title: Dharan’s Bhat-Bhateni to resume operations Wednesday
articles.summary: Bhat-Bhateni Super Store in Dharan will reopen its doors on Wednesday, Bhadra 24, according to COO Panu Paudel. The store, located on Putali Line, will resume regular services, reaffirming the company's commitment to modern facilities and quality service for customers.

articles.title: Iran conflict drives up fuel costs for US consumers
articles.summary: Disruptions to crude oil shipments caused by the Iran conflict and a blockage of a key maritime route have driven U.S. gasoline prices to $4.14 per gallon, the highest level in years. The surge in fuel costs is increasing financial pressure on American households and affecting travel plans across the country.

articles.title: Gen Z upended the old order. A year later, what has changed?
articles.summary: A year after a Gen Z-led protest on September 8, 2025, which disrupted Nepal's coalition government of the Nepali Congress and CPK-UML, the article examines the lasting impacts on the political landscape. It assesses whether the youth movement has led to policy shifts, changes in party dynamics, or a reconfiguration of power structures, and explores ongoing challenges and opportunities for reform in Kathmandu and beyond.

articles.title: Gripping drama of the transgender community
articles.summary: The Nepali film "Elephants in the Fog," a gripping drama centered on the transgender community, has garnered international acclaim after winning accolades at the Cannes Film Festival. The movie was recently screened in Kathmandu, drawing attention to both its artistic merit and its social themes. The screening highlights the growing prominence of Nepali cinema on the global stage and sparks conversations about transgender rights and representation in Nepal.

articles.title: Nepal tells tourists: ‘Your Visit Matters’
articles.summary: The Nepalese government is urging tourists to visit the country as a direct way to support its reconstruction efforts. By increasing tourist arrivals, Nepal hopes to boost its economy, generate revenue for rebuilding infrastructure, and showcase its cultural and natural attractions. The campaign emphasizes that each visitor’s presence contributes to the nation’s recovery and long‑term development.

articles.title: Preserving the diversity  of intangible heritage
articles.summary: The article discusses Nepal's newly drafted heritage legislation, emphasizing the need for an inclusive governing board to effectively protect the country's intangible cultural heritage. While the bill contains statutory language, critics argue that without diverse representation from various cultural groups, the board may fail to safeguard traditions, languages, and practices that define Nepal's rich cultural mosaic. The piece calls for broader stakeholder involvement to ensure the law translates into meaningful preservation efforts.

articles.title: The return of the Taleju necklace
articles.summary: After more than five years of diplomatic and legal efforts, Nepal is set to receive the historic Taleju necklace and several other cultural artefacts that were taken abroad decades ago. The necklace, a sacred object associated with the Taleju deity and the Kathmandu Valley's royal heritage, has been the focus of a sustained campaign by Nepalese officials, heritage activists, and international partners to secure its return. The successful negotiations highlight growing global attention to cultural restitution and are expected to boost national pride and tourism, while also prompting discussions on the preservation of Nepal's remaining heritage collections.
